title: Heading of Settings › Notifications: where socios (Socio's AI agents) reach the person when something needs them.
intro: "Socio" is the product name; "a socio" is one of its AI agents. "Channels" are the ways a notification can reach the person (push notifications, Telegram).
saved: Toast after a channel's setting saved.
channel.on: Label beside a channel's switch while the channel is on.
channel.off: Label beside a channel's switch while the channel is off.
channel.switch: Accessible name of a channel's on/off switch; {{channel}} is the channel's name, such as "Push notifications" or "Telegram".
channel.shows: Heading of the choice of how much a notification shows (the message, or only who needs you).
channel.goesTo: Where a channel delivers; {{targets}} is a list of names, such as a Telegram account.
channel.nowhere: Shown when a channel is on but has nowhere to deliver yet (no device, no linked account).
channel.telegramSettings: Link to the page where the person links their Telegram account. Telegram is a brand name.
content.private: A choice: the notification only says which socio needs the person. Keep “<socio> needs you” as a sample of the notification, with <socio> standing for a socio's name (it is not markup).
push.devices: Heading of the list of browsers and installed apps that get push notifications.
push.removeLabel: Accessible name of a device's Remove button; {{device}} is its name, such as "Chrome on Linux".
push.removed: Toast after a browser or app was removed from push notifications.
push.here: Shown when push notifications are already on in the browser the person is using.
push.turnOn: Button: ask the browser for permission and turn push notifications on in it.
push.notAllowed: "Allow" is the browser's own button in its permission prompt; use the word your language's browsers show.
push.ios: Apple only lets an installed web app (added to the Home Screen) get notifications on iPhone and iPad. Use Apple's own name for "Home Screen" in your language.
push.unsupported: Telegram is offered as the other channel.
test.title: Heading of the card that sends a test notification.
test.sent: Result of the test; {{channels}} is a list of per-channel results (see test.channel).
test.channel: One channel's test result: {{channel}} is its name, {{counts}} a short list such as "1 sent, 1 failed".
test.sentCount: How many devices or accounts the test reached on a channel.
test.failedCount: How many deliveries of the test failed on a channel.
issues.title: Heading of the card for issue subscriptions: one-time notices when a set of issues (on the team's Improvements board) all reach a status.
issues.keys: Label of the field for issue keys such as "CB-12" (a project prefix and a number).
issues.keysLabel: Accessible name of the issue keys field.
issues.status: Label of the select picking the status all the issues must reach (Done, In progress…).
issues.statusLabel: Accessible name of the status select.
issues.subscribe: Button: create a subscription that notifies once.
issues.alreadyMatched: The issues already have that status; a notice comes only after a later change brings them there again.
issues.target: After a subscription's issue keys: the status they are waiting for. {{status}} is a status name.
issues.unsubscribeLabel: Accessible name of a subscription's Unsubscribe button; {{issues}} is its issue keys, comma-separated.
issues.states.watching: A subscription's state: waiting for the issues to change.
issues.states.ready: A subscription's state: all issues match and the notice is about to be sent.
issues.states.triggered: A subscription's state: the notice was sent.
issues.states.cancelled: A subscription's state: the person unsubscribed.
